turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so we have twenty minutes, and I'd like to start with why my son found out about a zero on his phone in the middle of class. Who entered that mark, and did anyone speak to Owen first?
I'm waiting, Hale. You have my two questions.
Here is my offer. I will change the zero to 70 percent today if you drop the complaint and we never mention it again.

You're trading Owen a mark for my silence, and I'm writing that down word for word. "We never mention it again" is going upstairs to the principal with me unless you withdraw the zero outright, and you still haven't told me whether anyone spoke to Owen before it went in.
Nobody has to know. Do we have a deal?

No. "Nobody has to know" is going on my pad right under your offer, and the principal will know by five o'clock. Either the zero comes off with no conditions, or you show me what you actually have on Owen's essay.
